name: Chapter 14: Waves
description: Transverse and longitudinal waves, wave equation, wave speed on strings and in gases, superposition, reflection, standing waves, pipes, beats

cards.term: What is a wave?
cards.definition: A pattern of disturbance that moves without bulk flow of matter, carrying energy and information

cards.term: Why do cork pieces on a rippled pond not move outward?
cards.definition: Water only moves up and down locally; only the disturbance travels

cards.term: Three kinds of waves
cards.definition: Mechanical: yes — string, water, sound, seismic waves; Electromagnetic: no — light, radio, X-rays (speed c in vacuum); Matter waves: associated with electrons, protons, atoms (electron microscope)

cards.term: Speed of electromagnetic waves in vacuum?
cards.definition: c = 299 792 458 m/s (exact)

cards.term: How does a disturbance travel along coupled springs or train bogies?
cards.definition: Each part pushes the next through elastic coupling; each only oscillates about its own equilibrium

cards.term: What plays the role of the spring’s extension in a sound wave?
cards.definition: The change in density (and pressure): compressions and rarefactions

cards.term: Transverse vs longitudinal wave?
cards.definition: Transverse: particles oscillate ⟂ to the direction of travel (string). Longitudinal: particles oscillate along it (sound)

cards.term: A single jerk on a string produces…?
cards.definition: A transverse pulse

cards.term: How is a longitudinal wave produced in a pipe?
cards.definition: A piston pushed and pulled creates compressions and rarefactions travelling along the air

cards.term: Why can’t transverse waves travel through fluids?
cards.definition: They need a medium that resists shear; fluids cannot sustain shearing stress. Longitudinal waves need only compressibility (all media)

cards.term: Which waves can travel in steel? In air?
cards.definition: Steel: both transverse and longitudinal. Air: only longitudinal

cards.term: Capillary vs gravity water waves?
cards.definition: Capillary: ripples of a few cm, restoring force surface tension. Gravity: metres to hundreds of metres, restoring force gravity

cards.term: Ocean waves: transverse or longitudinal?
cards.definition: A combination: water particles move up–down and back–forth

cards.term: Wind vs sound wave?
cards.definition: Wind is motion of air as a whole; a sound wave is a moving pattern of compressions with no net flow

cards.term: Wave type examples (Example 14.1)
cards.definition: Kink in a spring from a sideways jerk: transverse and longitudinal; Piston moved back and forth in a liquid: longitudinal; Waves from a motorboat: transverse and longitudinal; Ultrasonic waves from a quartz crystal: longitudinal

cards.term: Equation of a harmonic wave travelling in +x?
cards.definition: \( y(x,t) = a\sin(kx - \omega t + \phi) \); for −x: \( a\sin(kx + \omega t + \phi) \)

cards.term: Symbols in y = a sin(kx − ωt + φ)
cards.definition: a: amplitude; k: angular wave number (rad/m); ω: angular frequency (rad/s); kx − ωt + φ: phase; φ: initial phase angle

cards.term: Fix t, then fix x in y = a sin(kx − ωt): what do you see?
cards.definition: Fixed t: the shape of the wave (a sine in x). Fixed x: that particle does SHM in time

cards.term: Define wavelength and angular wave number.
cards.definition: λ: least distance between points in the same phase (crest to crest). \( k = \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda} \)

cards.term: Relations for period and frequency of a wave?
cards.definition: \( \omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T} = 2\pi\nu \)

cards.term: Longitudinal wave: what does the displacement mean?
cards.definition: \( s(x,t) = a\sin(kx - \omega t + \phi) \) — displacement along the direction of travel

cards.term: Reading a wave equation

advancedHtml.frontHtml:

Find the missing step.

y = 0.005 sin(80.0x − 3.0t) (SI). Amplitude, wavelength, period, frequency?
  1. a = 0.005 m = 5 mm
  2. ?
  3. T = 2π/ω = 2.09 s
  4. ν = 1/T = 0.48 Hz
advancedHtml.backHtml:
Example 14.2

Find the missing step.

y = 0.005 sin(80.0x − 3.0t) (SI). Amplitude, wavelength, period, frequency?
  1. a = 0.005 m = 5 mm
  2. λ = 2π/k = 2π/80 = 7.85 cm
  3. T = 2π/ω = 2.09 s
  4. ν = 1/T = 0.48 Hz

cards.term: Phase difference between two points Δx apart on a wave?
cards.definition: \( \Delta\phi = \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda}\Delta x = k\,\Delta x \)

cards.term: Wave speed in terms of ω, k, λ, ν?
cards.definition: \( v = \dfrac{\omega}{k} = \lambda\nu = \dfrac{\lambda}{T} \): in one period the pattern moves one wavelength

cards.term: What sets the speed and what sets the frequency of a mechanical wave?
cards.definition: Speed: the medium (elasticity and inertia). Frequency: the source. Then λ = v/ν

cards.term: Speed of transverse waves on a stretched string?
cards.definition: \( v = \sqrt{\dfrac{T}{\mu}} \) (T = tension, μ = mass per unit length)

cards.term: How is v = √(T/μ) found in NCERT?
cards.definition: By dimensional analysis (the constant C = 1 comes from the exact theory)

cards.term: Example 14.3: steel wire 0.72 m, 5.0 g, tension 60 N. Wave speed?
cards.definition: μ = 6.9 × 10⁻³ kg/m → v = ≈ 93 m/s

cards.term: Speed of longitudinal (sound) waves in a fluid and in a solid bar?
cards.definition: \( v = \sqrt{\dfrac{B}{\rho}} \) (fluid); \( v = \sqrt{\dfrac{Y}{\rho}} \) (thin bar)

cards.term: Why is sound faster in solids and liquids than in gases?
cards.definition: They are denser, but their elastic moduli are far larger

cards.term: Speed of sound in air (0 °C), water, steel (Table 14.1)?
cards.definition: Air 331 m/s, water ≈ 1402–1482 m/s, steel 5941 m/s

cards.term: Newton’s formula for sound in a gas, and its value for air?
cards.definition: \( v = \sqrt{\dfrac{P}{\rho}} \) (isothermal, B = P) → 280 m/s: about 15 % too low

cards.term: What was the Laplace correction?
cards.definition: Sound compressions are too fast for heat flow → adiabatic, B = γP: \( v = \sqrt{\dfrac{\gamma P}{\rho}} \) ≈ 331 m/s

cards.term: Exercise 14.4: speed of sound in air vs pressure, temperature, humidity?
cards.definition: \( v = \sqrt{\gamma RT/M} \): independent of pressure ∝ √T increases with humidity (water vapour lowers M)

cards.term: Does the speed of a mechanical wave depend on the source’s velocity?
cards.definition: No: relative to the medium it depends only on the medium

cards.term: Exercise 14.1: 2.50 kg, 20.0 m string under 200 N. Time for a jerk to travel its length?
cards.definition: v = √(200/0.125) = 40 m/s → 0.5 s

cards.term: Exercise 14.2: stone dropped from a 300 m tower. When is the splash heard at the top (sound 340 m/s)?
cards.definition: 7.82 s fall + 0.88 s sound ≈ 8.7 s

cards.term: Exercise 14.3: 12.0 m, 2.10 kg steel wire. Tension for wave speed 343 m/s?
cards.definition: T = μv² ≈ 2.06 × 10⁴ N

cards.term: Exercise 14.6: 1000 kHz bat sound hits water. Wavelength reflected (air 340 m/s) and transmitted (water 1486 m/s)?
cards.definition: 3.4 × 10⁻⁴ m and 1.49 × 10⁻³ m (frequency is unchanged)

cards.term: Exercise 14.7: ultrasonic scanner 4.2 MHz in tissue (1.7 km/s). Wavelength?
cards.definition: 4.1 × 10⁻⁴ m

cards.term: Exercise 14.8: y = 3.0 sin(36t + 0.018x + π/4) (cm, s). Direction, speed, frequency, λ?
cards.definition: Travels right to left at 20 m/s; a = 3.0 cm, ν ≈ 5.7 Hz, φ = π/4, λ ≈ 3.5 m

cards.term: Exercise 14.10: y = 2.0 cos 2π(10t − 0.0080x + 0.35) (cm). Phase difference for points 4 m and 0.5 m apart?
cards.definition: 6.4π rad and 0.8π rad for λ/2: π for 3λ/4: 3π/2 (the key writes π/2, the same phase counted the other way round)

cards.term: Exercise 14.5: must every function of (x ± vt) represent a travelling wave?
cards.definition: No: it must also be finite everywhere, always; of (x − vt)², log[(x + vt)/x₀], 1/(x + vt), none qualifies

cards.text: Principle of superposition: when waves overlap, the resultant displacement is the {{c1::algebraic sum}} of the individual displacements; each wave moves {{c2::as if the others were absent}}.

cards.term: Two equal and opposite pulses cross. What happens at the moment of full overlap? After?
cards.definition: Displacement is zero everywhere for an instant; afterwards both pulses continue unchanged

cards.term: Two identical waves with phase difference φ: resultant amplitude?
cards.definition: \( A = 2a\cos\dfrac{\phi}{2} \)

cards.term: Constructive vs destructive interference?
cards.definition: Constructive: φ = 0, 2π… → amplitude 2a. Destructive: φ = π → amplitude 0

cards.term: Reflection at a rigid boundary vs an open (free) boundary?
cards.definition: Rigid: phase change of π (pulse inverted). Free: no phase change

cards.term: Why is a pulse inverted at a rigid wall?
cards.definition: The end cannot move, so incident + reflected must cancel there; also the wall pulls back on the string (third law)

cards.term: Correction: NCERT Eqs. (14.35)–(14.36) write the reflected wave as a sin(kx − ωt ± …). What is right?
cards.definition: A reflected wave travels the other way: \( y_r = -a\sin(kx + \omega t) \) (rigid) or \( +a\sin(kx + \omega t) \) (open), as NCERT’s own summary states

cards.term: Examples of rigid and open reflection?
cards.definition: Rigid: echo, string tied to a wall. Open: string on a freely sliding ring, open end of an organ pipe

cards.term: Equation of a stationary wave?
cards.definition: \( y = 2a\sin kx\,\cos\omega t \): kx and ωt appear separately

cards.term: Stationary wave: nodes, antinodes and phase
cards.definition: Nodes stay at rest, antinodes have maximum amplitude, nodes are λ/2 apart; points within a loop move in phase, adjacent loops opposite

advancedHtml.frontHtml:
Stationary waves · string

A string fixed at both ends vibrates in a stationary wave. What do the nodes and antinodes do, and are the points in phase?

Pluck, then watch one point.

cards.term: Positions of nodes and antinodes?
cards.definition: Nodes: \( x = \dfrac{n\lambda}{2} \); antinodes: \( x = \left(n + \tfrac12\right)\dfrac{\lambda}{2} \); each set is λ/2 apart

cards.term: Progressive vs stationary waves
cards.definition: Progressive wave: amplitude: same; Progressive wave: phase: different; Stationary wave: amplitude: different (0 at nodes); Stationary wave: phase (within a loop): same

advancedHtml.frontHtml:

cards.term: String of length L fixed at both ends: allowed wavelengths and frequencies?
cards.definition: \( \lambda_n = \dfrac{2L}{n},\quad \nu_n = \dfrac{nv}{2L} \), n = 1, 2, 3… (all harmonics)

cards.term: Fundamental of a string fixed at both ends?
cards.definition: \( \nu_1 = \dfrac{v}{2L} = \dfrac{1}{2L}\sqrt{\dfrac T\mu} \)

cards.term: Why do a violin and a sitar playing the same note sound different?
cards.definition: They excite different mixtures of harmonics (timbre / quality)

cards.term: Pipe closed at one end: allowed frequencies?
cards.definition: \( \nu = \left(n + \tfrac12\right)\dfrac{v}{2L} \): fundamental \( \dfrac{v}{4L} \), then only odd harmonics (3, 5, 7…)

cards.term: Identify the higher modes of a closed pipe.
cards.definition: Seventh, ninth, eleventh harmonics: still only odd multiples, closed end a node, open end an antinode

cards.term: Pipe open at both ends: allowed frequencies?
cards.definition: \( \nu_n = \dfrac{nv}{2L} \): all harmonics; both ends antinodes

cards.term: Mnemonic for pipes?
cards.definition: "Closed is Odd": closed pipe → v/4L and odd harmonics; open pipe and string → v/2L and all harmonics

cards.term: In a sound wave, why is a displacement node a pressure antinode?
cards.definition: Where air cannot move, neighbouring layers push in and pull away → largest pressure change (Exercise 14.19a)

cards.term: Example 14.5: 30.0 cm pipe open at both ends, source 1.1 kHz (v = 330 m/s). Which mode? And with one end closed?
cards.definition: Open: νₙ = 550n → 2nd harmonic. Closed: 275 Hz × odd only; 1.1 kHz = 4th → no resonance

cards.term: What is resonance for strings and pipes?
cards.definition: Large response when a driving frequency matches a natural (normal-mode) frequency

cards.term: Exercise 14.11: y = 0.06 sin(2πx/3) cos(120πt), 1.5 m, 30 g string. λ, ν, v of the component waves and the tension?
cards.definition: λ = 3 m, ν = 60 Hz, v = 180 m/s; T = μv² = 648 N

cards.term: Exercise 14.12: on that string, do all points have the same frequency, phase, amplitude? Amplitude at 0.375 m?
cards.definition: Same frequency and phase (except nodes), different amplitudes; at 0.375 m: 0.06 sin(π/4) ≈ 0.042 m

cards.term: Correction: NCERT Exercise 14.12 refers to "Exercise 15.11". Which one?
cards.definition: Exercise 14.11

cards.term: Exercise 14.14: wire in its fundamental at 45 Hz, mass 3.5 × 10⁻² kg, μ = 4.0 × 10⁻² kg/m. Speed and tension?
cards.definition: L = 0.875 m → v = 2Lν ≈ 79 m/s; T = μv² ≈ 248 N

cards.term: Exercise 14.15: resonance tube with a 340 Hz fork resonates at 25.5 cm. Speed of sound?
cards.definition: L = λ/4 → λ = 1.02 m → v ≈ 347 m/s

cards.term: Exercise 14.16: 100 cm steel rod clamped at the middle; fundamental 2.53 kHz. Speed of sound in steel?
cards.definition: Ends are antinodes, middle a node: L = λ/2 → v = 2 × 2530 = 5.06 km/s

cards.term: Exercise 14.17: 20 cm pipe closed at one end, 430 Hz source (v = 340 m/s). Which mode? Open at both ends?
cards.definition: Fundamental (340/0.8 ≈ 425 Hz); with both ends open (850 Hz) no resonance

cards.term: What are beats?
cards.definition: Periodic waxing and waning of loudness when two sounds of slightly different frequencies are heard together

cards.term: Beat frequency?
Resultant of two nearly equal frequencies?
cards.definition: \( s = [2a\cos\omega_b t]\cos\omega_a t \): oscillates at the average frequency with a slowly varying amplitude

cards.term: How do musicians use beats?
cards.definition: To tune instruments: adjust until the beats disappear

cards.term: Example 14.6: A (427 Hz) and B give 5 beats/s; tightening B reduces beats to 3/s. Original frequency of B?
cards.definition: Tightening raises νB and beats fall, so νB < νA: 422 Hz

cards.term: Exercise 14.18: A (324 Hz) and B give 6 beats/s; loosening A reduces beats to 3/s. Frequency of B?
cards.definition: Loosening lowers A and beats fall, so A > B: 318 Hz

cards.term: What are the musical pillars of the Nellaiappar temple?
cards.definition: Stone pillars (7th century, Tamil Nadu) that give the notes of Indian music when tapped; their vibrations depend on elasticity, density and shape

cards.term: Classify the wave functions (Exercise 14.13)
cards.definition: y = 2 cos(3x) sin(10t): stationary; (b) the function that blows up at x + vt = 0: none: not an acceptable wave; y = 3 sin(5x − 0.5t) + 4 cos(5x − 0.5t): travelling harmonic wave; y = cos x sin t + cos 2x sin 2t: sum of two stationary waves

cards.term: Exercise 14.19(b): how do bats locate obstacles without eyes?
cards.definition: Echolocation: they emit ultrasound and use the delay and change of the reflected waves

cards.term: Exercise 14.19(e): why does a pulse change shape in a dispersive medium?
cards.definition: Its component frequencies travel at different speeds

cards.term: Chapter 14 formula sheet
cards.definition: Wave speed: v = νλ = ω/k; String: v = √(T/μ); Sound in a gas: v = √(γP/ρ); String / open pipe: νₙ = nv/2L; Closed pipe: ν = (2n + 1)v/4L; Beats: ν₁ − ν₂
